relevance.rationale: NOT an orphan -- correcting the slice's premise. folio/schema/references.ts already carries an entry whose note names this exact PDF (registered 2026-08-08). But it is a bib orphan: no citation site in any .md and no Lean -- Ref: anywhere in content/. The paper studies multiple polylogarithm values at Nth roots of unity, generating relations among same-weight, same-level MPVs from four families (regularized double shuffle, regularized distribution, lifted lower-weight, and weight-one relations), calling those 'standard', and conjecturing the dichotomy that for standard levels N = 1, 2, 3 or N = p^n with p >= 5 the standard relations produce all linear relations (improving the Deligne-Goncharov dimension bound for N > 3), while otherwise non-standard relations exist. Level 5 is standard. That bears directly on conj:cl3-zeta5-geometric-realization, which lists candidate closed forms for the depth-3 Bring trilogarithm Cl_3(2 pi / 5) -- a weight-3, level-5 MPV -- since the standard relations plus the improved dimension bound constrain how many independent candidates that space can support. The existing reference note already names that block as the target; the citation was simply never made.

keyResults.locator: the standard-relations framework + the level dichotomy (abstract, and the d(w,N) discussion)
keyResults.statement: For standard levels (N = 1, 2, 3 or p^n with p >= 5) the four families of standard relations are conjectured to generate all Q-linear relations among MPVs of a given weight and level, improving the Deligne-Goncharov lower bound on d(w,N) for N > 3.
keyResults.useForFolio: Bounds the dimension of the weight-3, level-5 MPV space in which the Cl_3(2 pi / 5) closed-form candidates live, which is what conj:cl3-zeta5-geometric-realization enumerates without a stated independence bound.

proposedActions.rationale: The reference exists and its own note names this block as the intended consumer, but no block cites it; the candidates list currently enumerates weight-3 level-5 forms with no relation-space bound.

The corpus has a PSLQ independence probe for the same zeta_5 target; the paper's standard-relation count for weight 3, level 5 is an independent bound to check the probe's basis against. A bound to cross-check, not a value to adopt.
